questions.question_text: Which lane should you normally use on a three-lane motorway?
questions.explanation: You should always drive in the left-hand lane unless you are overtaking slower traffic.

questions.question_text: Which lane should you normally use when driving on a three-lane motorway?
questions.explanation: You should always stay in the left-hand lane unless you are overtaking other vehicles.

questions.question_text: What is the national speed limit for a car on a motorway?
questions.explanation: The national speed limit for cars on motorways is 70 mph.

questions.question_text: What is the national speed limit for a standard car on a motorway?
questions.explanation: The national speed limit for cars on motorways in the UK is 70 mph.

questions.question_text: What should you do if you become tired while driving on a motorway?
options: Keep driving but reduce your speed
Exit at the next service area and take a break
Open the windows for fresh air and continue
Move to the hard shoulder to sleep
questions.explanation: Motorways are high-speed environments; if you are tired, you must stop at a designated rest area immediately.

questions.question_text: What is the maximum speed limit for a car on a motorway?
questions.explanation: The national speed limit for cars driving on a motorway in the UK is 70 mph.

questions.question_text: If you start feeling tired while driving on a motorway, what is the safest action?
options: Drive to the next service station to take a rest
Turn the air conditioning up high
Continue driving at a slower speed
questions.explanation: Tiredness can impair your judgement significantly; resting at a service station is the only way to recover sufficiently to continue.
